**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Gold remained under pressure from margin calls, risk aversion, declining equity values at the start of the week, and like all metals in the precious complex, the resulting long liquidation. This affected the other metals too, of course, with declines of -8 % in gold exceeded by –15 % silver, and declines of - 12 and -10 % in Platinum and Palladium respectively, using the 20-27 Fixing prices. Gold responded to margin call pressure, whereas the remaining three were caught more directly in the perception of economic risk. • Some really substantial COTR declines have been witnessed. Huge liquidation from COMEX silver longs (over 92 million Tozs) may start to encourage money back into the metal as we have fallen back to about 44 % of the positioning seen roughly a year ago. Gold’s decline in long positioning of over 5 million ounces was reminiscent of the sell-offs seen in the Lehman fall-out-as tension over Greece ratchets up to ever higher levels of anxiety. • The week to the 30th of September saw declines in all ETF positions with the exception of silver— demonstrating that perhaps stickier money recognises the decline in length elsewhere is overdone? It certainly underscores the resilience of silver’s true believers. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **03 October 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **03 October 2011** ## **Gold CFTC data to 27 September 2011; ETF data to 30 September 2011.** ### **Exchange (COMEX) and ETF Silver Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**|_Futures_||_Options_||**Net Total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**Date**|**Open**

e**|**4,089,037**|**-284,262**|**354,477**|**-745,050**|**-340,000**|**3,074,202**|| - Last week saw gold make a low of $1535 basis December futures in a massive ‘risk off’ move which saw strong declines in equity markets and selling pressure as gold was sold to pay for margin required elsewhere. Once again, although counter-intuitive to outsiders, gold was functioning as a store of value to be drawn upon in a crisis, as the KOSPI made a low of 1644 and the HIS (Hang Seng) plunged to a low of 16,999 overnight on the Monday. The remainder of the week saw gold recover in a rather weak fashion and fail to breach the 38.2 Fibonacci retracement of the drop from the highs. We would like to see a daily close back above that point, US$1678, and a close on the dailies above US$1782 would demonstrate a rejection of the September decline. As the price dropped, signs of good physical demand in Asia emerged, and with no resolution of the Greek crisis, and continuing slow growth, the path for this week looks to be ‘recovery’ or ‘base-building. - Net long speculative positions in gold fell by 5.20 million Tozs on COMEX, a substantial drop which, scrolling back through the data, remains unmatched until we get back to the week of the 12th August 2008, when a 5.111 million tozs draw-down in net longs occurred, at approximately half of today’s US$ gold prices. This leaves net longs at 19.975 million, compared with the high of the year at 33.079 reported on the 2nd of August, a 13.10 million toz decline that leaves the core position 60 % of that maximum length. A healthy clear-out, possibly. In Japan, investors added 136,000 Tozs to their longs. - Gold ETF positions fell by 815,000 ounces in the week to the 30th of September, falling to 67.10 million ounces, as expected given the recent price drops. Redemptions have not been universal however, demonstrating the stickiness of ETF holdings. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—September 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

**Net**||**$/oz**| |**20-Sep-11**|1,920,400|1,192,000|316,300|**1,508,300**|**384,981**|1,893,281|1,774.00| |**27-Sep-11**|1,885,400|1,043,350|187,600|**1,230,950**|**323,369**|1,554,319|1,568.00| |**Change**|**-35,000**|**-148,650**|**-128,700**|**-277,350**|**-61,612**|**-338,962**|**-206.00**| ||**ETFs**||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**23-Sep-11**|359,127|476,643|481,033|88,490|120,346|**1,525,639**|| |**30-Sep-11**|356,610|478,573|461,691|86,490|120,346|**1,503,710**|| |**Change**|**-2,517**|**1,930**|**-19,342**|**-2,000**|**0**|**-21,929**|| - Silver dropped to a mind-bending low of $26.12 (December futures) last Monday, as part of fierce long liquidation. Since then we have seen cautious recovery, although the important 38.20 Fibonacci retracement at $32.76 was only threatened briefly, when silver then proceeded to drop almost $2 from the open, $2.75 from the high. Trying to trade silver last week was a punishing experience for most. Looking forward, resistance comes in at $36.86 and the $38 level. However, the rally off the lows still leaves the way open to $55 as far as the recent lows are not seen again. With weak Core Durable goods (-0.10 % compared with a forecast of 0.1 % and 0.70 % previously) The middle of the week was tough news-wise for silver, but an improving Chicago PMI at the end of the week might have flattered the ‘industrial’ side of silver. The target on the Gold-Silver ratio to 61 has been met, and the next target is 67 should gold out-perform, however, through 50, we see a possibility for the ratio to retest 40. - Silver speculative longs dropped by over 92 million tozs between the 20th and the 27th of September. A year ago, silver net longs stood at 342.49 million tozs, with the price at just under $21. Longs now stand at 151.25 million ounces, a scant 44 % of that position. There is plenty of scope to re-build investment length if events create a renewal of interest in silver. - Over 3 million Tozs of ETF length was added last week—that side of the community clearly do not think silver is ‘over’ and rather see the price drop as a dip to be bought into. #### **Silver Exchange Investment, April 09—September 11** 450 50 Silver price, $/oz

What was notable was that of all the net volume since Jan 2011, totalling 13,280 kilos, 14 % of that volume was seen last week, with 362 kilos per trading day compared to a daily average of around 70-75 for the year so far. Some evidence of light consumer demand was seen as the price dropped. Technically, $1635 looks like the upside price challenge to beat on any rebound. 2,500 2,000

Just over one week later, and we are well on our way to achieving that measured target with today’s dip through $600. Almost exactly one year ago in October 2010, a period of congestion between $577 and $595 in spot palladium took place and this level may well prove to be interim support in this vertiginous fall. $653 is the level above us where decent resistance lies in the event of a counter-trend rally. Overall, although the recent price action by palladium looks (and is) terrible, we may be close to intermediate levels of support , although crucially with no sign of a definitive ‘buy’ signal. 2,000 1,000

- Net long speculative positions in palladium on NYMEX fell for another week, with a decline of 374,000 tozs. The total longs now stand at 677,500 Tozs, compared to the recent length at the beginning of August of 1,887,000 tozs. We are now at about 36 % of that figure, and notwithstanding the anxiety over the world economic outlook, and the penalty paid by recent longs, the tremendous decline in the net long position is in itself a potentially positive figure for Palladium in the medium term. #### **Palladium ETF Investment, Apr 07—September 11** 2,500
